newsitem.title: CHINA: FOCUS - HK properties in vogue, lead stocks to record.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HK properties in vogue, lead stocks to record.

text.p: Property stocks were back in vogue on Thursday, leading Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index to a record high as investors shrugged off recent worries about the sector and looked forward to healthy property market growth. "People are quite optimistic about a rebound in residential property prices in the next few months. Property stocks tend to move ahead of the prices of residential units," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research.

The Hang Seng Index soared 382.53 points, or 2.39 percent, to a record high of 16,365.71 points on Thursday, led by a 4.10 percent surge in the properties sub-index to 27,116.55 points. Property stocks have underperformed the blue chip Hang Seng Index this year, plagued by uncertainty over how the government will tackle escalating real estate prices.

As Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa took over leadership of the former British territory on July 1, when Hong Kong was handed back to China, he vowed to tackle exorbitant real estate prices with an increase in housing supply.

Prices in the real estate market have dropped about five percent since the end of June after surging about 30 percent during the first half of the year, with buyers scurrying out of the market fearing punitive measures against speculators.

But analysts said the property market was looking healthier, with end-user demand still strong and property developers likely to see strong earnings growth for years to come as they benefited from an increase in sales volumes.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd sold all 894 units on offer at its residential development Vista Paradiso in the New Territories on the first sale day last weekend.
Swire Pacific Ltd raised the number of flats on offer at its upmarket development The Floridian on Hong Kong Island this week due to a strong interest from potential buyers.
"I think people are seeing huge end-user demand without the speculators. Prices are stable. This is the perfect scenario," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority gave investors reason to be more optimistic earlier this week when it said that gross new loans had dropped two percent in June to HK$25.5 billion from May and that a tightening in mortgage lending seemed unnecessary given a recent cooling in the property market.

"Firstly, it appears that some concern over speculative interest in the market has now died down. Second to that is, the level of lending is actually slowing which is pretty positive. Thirdly, there is a recognition that affordability has actually improved," said Lehman Brothers property analyst Michael Leary.

"I think everybody realises that there is a housing shortage and therefore it is a question of not whether prices are going to go up or not, but by how much," said Leary, adding that he saw residential property prices rising about 10 percent over the coming 12 months.

Analysts said Hong Kong's property developers should continue to produce sturdy earnings over coming years, outstripping growth in other sectors. "At least for the next three to four years you are going to see good growth of about Analysts said Hong Kong's property developers should continue to produce sturdy earnings over coming years, outstripping growth in other sectors. "At least for the next three to four years you are going to see good growth of about 15 to 20 percent by the larger developers," said Leary.

"In the past, it has been very much price growth which has driven the earnings picture for the developers and now volume is becoming key. That is going to be a critical aspect of sustaining growth which is what we are projecting for Sun Hung Kai Properties, Henderson Land and Cheung Kong," he said.
Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd rose HK$1.75 to HK$97.25 on Thursday, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd gained HK$3.75 to HK$75.50 and Cheung Kong gained HK$5.25 to HK$86.00.
